claim: Trisomy 21 (T21) is the most common chromosomal abnormality in the human population, occurring in approximately 1 in 700 live births.
source: Trisomy 21 (T21) is the most common chromosomal abnormality in the human population, occurring in approximately 1 in 700 live births (Alexander et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Alexander et al., 2016

claim: The extra copy of chromosome 21 impacts human development in diverse ways across every major organ system, causing the condition known as Down syndrome.
source: The extra copy of chromosome 21 (chr21) impacts human development in diverse ways across every major organ system, causing the condition known as Down syndrome (DS).
evidence: Established scientific knowledge about Down syndrome

claim: Trisomy 21 protects individuals with Down syndrome from some diseases such as solid tumors and hypertension.
source: One of the most intriguing aspects of T21 is that it causes an altered disease spectrum in the population with DS, protecting these individuals from some diseases (e.g. solid tumors, hypertension), while strongly predisposing them to others (e.g. Alzheimer's disease, leukemia, autoimmune disorders) (Alexander et al., 2016; Sobey et al., 2015; Bratman et al., 2014; Roberts and Izraeli, 2014; Anwar et al., 1998; Malinge et al., 2013; Hasle et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: Trisomy 21 strongly predisposes individuals with Down syndrome to Alzheimer's disease, leukemia, and autoimmune disorders.
source: One of the most intriguing aspects of T21 is that it causes an altered disease spectrum in the population with DS, protecting these individuals from some diseases (e.g. solid tumors, hypertension), while strongly predisposing them to others (e.g. Alzheimer's disease, leukemia, autoimmune disorders) (Alexander et al., 2016; Sobey et al., 2015; Bratman et al., 2014; Roberts and Izraeli, 2014; Anwar et al., 1998; Malinge et al., 2013; Hasle et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: APP has been implicated in the development of Alzheimer's disease in Down syndrome.
source: A few chr21-encoded genes have been implicated in the development of specific comorbidities, such as APP in Alzheimer's disease (Wiseman et al., 2015), and DYRK1A and ERG in hematopoietic malignancies (Stankiewicz and Crispino, 2013; Malinge et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wiseman et al., 2015

claim: DYRK1A and ERG have been implicated in hematopoietic malignancies in Down syndrome.
source: A few chr21-encoded genes have been implicated in the development of specific comorbidities, such as APP in Alzheimer's disease (Wiseman et al., 2015), and DYRK1A and ERG in hematopoietic malignancies (Stankiewicz and Crispino, 2013; Malinge et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Stankiewicz and Crispino, 2013; Malinge et al., 2012

claim: The clinical manifestation of Down syndrome is highly variable among affected individuals.
source: The clinical manifestation of DS is highly variable among affected individuals, with various comorbidities appearing in a seemingly random fashion, suggesting the presence of strong modifiers, genetic or otherwise, of the deleterious effects of T21.
evidence: Established clinical observation

claim: Cognitive impairment in Down syndrome displays wide quantitative variation.
source: Even conserved features, such as cognitive impairment, display wide quantitative variation (de Sola et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to de Sola et al., 2015

claim: The mechanisms driving inter-individual variation in the population with Down syndrome are minimally understood.
source: Collectively, our understanding of the mechanisms driving such inter-individual variation in the population with DS is minimal.
evidence: Assessment of current state of knowledge

claim: It is unclear what gene expression changes are consistently caused by T21 versus those that are context-dependent.
source: More specifically, it is unclear what gene expression changes are consistently caused by T21, versus those that are context-dependent.
evidence: Assessment of current state of knowledge

claim: Integrated analyses of studies have indicated that changes in gene expression caused by T21 involve various signaling pathways.
source: Integrated analyses of a large body of studies have indicated that the changes in gene expression caused by T21 involve various signaling pathways (Scarpato et al., 2014), however, these studies vary widely in cell type, number of samples, and even analysis platform, among other variables (Volk et al., 2013; Costa et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Scarpato et al., 2014; Volk et al., 2013; Costa et al., 2011

claim: Gene expression analysis of cells from discordant monozygotic twins concluded that global gene expression changes in T21 cells are driven by differences in chromatin topology.
source: More recently, gene expression analysis of cells derived from discordant monozygotic twins, only one of which was affected by T21, concluded that global gene expression changes in T21 cells are driven by differences in chromatin topology, whereby affected genes are clustered into large chromosomal domains of activation or repression (Letourneau et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Letourneau et al., 2014

claim: Independent re-analysis of the Letourneau et al. data has challenged the conclusion about chromatin topology.
source: However, independent re-analysis of these data has challenged this conclusion (Do et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Do et al., 2015

claim: RNA-seq transcriptome analysis identified consistent gene expression signatures associated with T21 in all cell types examined.
source: Our RNA-seq transcriptome analysis identified consistent gene expression signatures associated with T21 in all cell types examined.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from RNA-seq analysis

claim: The fraction of the T21 gene expression signature not encoded on chr21 is dominated by the interferon transcriptional response.
source: Interestingly, the fraction of this gene expression signature that is not encoded on chr21 is dominated by the interferon (IFN) transcriptional response, an observation that is reproducible in skin fibroblasts, B cell-derived lymphoblastoid cell lines, as well as primary monocytes and T cells.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from RNA-seq analysis across multiple cell types

claim: The interferon transcriptional response is reproducible in skin fibroblasts, B cell-derived lymphoblastoid cell lines, as well as primary monocytes and T cells.
source: Interestingly, the fraction of this gene expression signature that is not encoded on chr21 is dominated by the interferon (IFN) transcriptional response, an observation that is reproducible in skin fibroblasts, B cell-derived lymphoblastoid cell lines, as well as primary monocytes and T cells.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from RNA-seq analysis across multiple cell types

claim: A kinome-focused shRNA screen identified JAK1 and TYK2 as strong negative regulators of T21 cell proliferation in fibroblasts.
source: In parallel, we performed a kinome-focused shRNA screen that identified the IFN-activated kinases JAK1 and TYK2 as strong negative regulators of T21 cell proliferation in fibroblasts.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from shRNA screen

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of JAK kinases improves T21 cell viability.
source: Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of JAK kinases improves T21 cell viability.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from drug treatment experiments

claim: Four interferon receptor subunits are encoded on chromosome 21.
source: Therefore, we propose that interferon activation, likely via increased gene dosage of the four interferon receptors encoded on chromosome 21, contributes to many of the clinical impacts of trisomy 21, and that interferon antagonists could have therapeutic benefits.
evidence: Established genomic knowledge

claim: Interferon activation likely occurs via increased gene dosage of the four interferon receptors encoded on chromosome 21.
source: Therefore, we propose that interferon activation, likely via increased gene dosage of the four interferon receptors encoded on chromosome 21, contributes to many of the clinical impacts of trisomy 21, and that interferon antagonists could have therapeutic benefits.
evidence: Logical inference from experimental data showing upregulation of chr21-encoded IFN receptors

claim: Interferon activation contributes to many of the clinical impacts of trisomy 21.
source: Therefore, we propose that interferon activation, likely via increased gene dosage of the four interferon receptors encoded on chromosome 21, contributes to many of the clinical impacts of trisomy 21, and that interferon antagonists could have therapeutic benefits.
evidence: Speculative proposal based on experimental findings

claim: Interferon antagonists could have therapeutic benefits for trisomy 21.
source: Therefore, we propose that interferon activation, likely via increased gene dosage of the four interferon receptors encoded on chromosome 21, contributes to many of the clinical impacts of trisomy 21, and that interferon antagonists could have therapeutic benefits.
evidence: Speculative proposal based on experimental findings

claim: Comparison of all T21 versus all D21 fibroblast cells identified 662 consistent differentially expressed genes.
source: In contrast, comparison of all T21 versus all D21 cells identified 662 consistent DEGs, with a disproportionate number of these upregulated in T21 cells (471 of 662, Figure 1A, T21 vs. D21, Supplementary file 1A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from RNA-seq analysis

claim: 471 of 662 differentially expressed genes are upregulated in T21 fibroblast cells.
source: In contrast, comparison of all T21 versus all D21 cells identified 662 consistent DEGs, with a disproportionate number of these upregulated in T21 cells (471 of 662, Figure 1A, T21 vs. D21, Supplementary file 1A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from RNA-seq analysis

claim: 88% of differentially expressed genes in T21 fibroblasts are located on chromosomes other than chromosome 21.
source: However, 88% of DEGs are located on other chromosomes, indicating the existence of conserved mechanisms driving these genome-wide changes in gene expression (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from RNA-seq analysis

claim: The existence of conserved mechanisms drives genome-wide changes in gene expression in T21 cells.
source: However, 88% of DEGs are located on other chromosomes, indicating the existence of conserved mechanisms driving these genome-wide changes in gene expression (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Logical inference from the observation that most DEGs are not on chr21

claim: The fraction of chr21-encoded differentially expressed genes increases steadily with sample size.
source: Of note, when we performed RNA-seq analysis using increasing numbers of T21 vs. D21 pairs, the fraction of chr21-encoded DEGs increased steadily with sample size, accounting for ~12% of the core gene expression signature in the 12 cell line panel.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from RNA-seq analysis with varying sample sizes

claim: Chr21-encoded differentially expressed genes account for approximately 12% of the core gene expression signature in the 12 cell line panel.
source: Of note, when we performed RNA-seq analysis using increasing numbers of T21 vs. D21 pairs, the fraction of chr21-encoded DEGs increased steadily with sample size, accounting for ~12% of the core gene expression signature in the 12 cell line panel.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from RNA-seq analysis

claim: The analysis did not reveal obvious contiguous domains of up- or downregulation across the genome.
source: This exercise revealed broad distribution across all chromosomes, with no obvious contiguous domains of up- or downregulation (see Figure 1—figure supplement 2A for a whole genome Manhattan plot, and Figure 1—figure supplement 3 for individual chromosomes).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from RNA-seq analysis and visualization in Manhattan plots

claim: Visual analysis of differentially expressed genes from individual chromosomes did not reveal large dysregulated domains previously claimed by Letourneau et al.
source: In fact, mere visual analysis of DEGs from the individual chromosomes previously claimed by Letourneau et al. to harbor large dysregulated domains (e.g. chr3, chr11, chr19) did not reveal such domains in our dataset, showing instead obvious regions of overlapping activation and repression (shaded gray boxes in Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from RNA-seq analysis and comparison with previous study

claim: The analysis is consistent with the report that re-analyzed the Letourneau et al. data and questioned the existence of chromosomal domains.
source: Thus, our analysis is more consistent with the report that re-analyzed the data in Letournaeu et al. and questioned the existence of these chromosomal domains (Do et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by experimental data and citation to Do et al., 2015

claim: The only region of the genome with clear contiguous upregulation of differentially expressed genes was chromosome 21 itself.
source: In fact, the only region of the genome at which there was clear contiguous upregulation of DEGs was chr21 itself (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplements 2A and 3).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from RNA-seq analysis and visualization in Manhattan plots

claim: Chr21 differentially expressed genes are regulated mostly by increased gene dosage.
source: In order to characterize the mechanism driving the consistent changes caused by T21, we examined the regulatory differences between DEGs encoded on chr21 and those not encoded on chr21. Several lines of evidence indicate that, while chr21 DEGs are regulated mostly by increased gene dosage, non-chr21 DEGs may be driven by specific pathways that are subject to signal amplification, with a bias toward upregulation, and greatly affected by inter-individual variation.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing ~1.5-fold upregulation of chr21 genes

claim: Non-chr21 differentially expressed genes may be driven by specific pathways that are subject to signal amplification.
source: In order to characterize the mechanism driving the consistent changes caused by T21, we examined the regulatory differences between DEGs encoded on chr21 and those not encoded on chr21. Several lines of evidence indicate that, while chr21 DEGs are regulated mostly by increased gene dosage, non-chr21 DEGs may be driven by specific pathways that are subject to signal amplification, with a bias toward upregulation, and greatly affected by inter-individual variation.
evidence: Logical inference from experimental data showing larger fold changes and greater variation in non-chr21 DEGs

claim: Non-chr21 differentially expressed genes show a bias toward upregulation.
source: In order to characterize the mechanism driving the consistent changes caused by T21, we examined the regulatory differences between DEGs encoded on chr21 and those not encoded on chr21. Several lines of evidence indicate that, while chr21 DEGs are regulated mostly by increased gene dosage, non-chr21 DEGs may be driven by specific pathways that are subject to signal amplification, with a bias toward upregulation, and greatly affected by inter-individual variation.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from RNA-seq analysis

claim: Non-chr21 differentially expressed genes are greatly affected by inter-individual variation.
source: In order to characterize the mechanism driving the consistent changes caused by T21, we examined the regulatory differences between DEGs encoded on chr21 and those not encoded on chr21. Several lines of evidence indicate that, while chr21 DEGs are regulated mostly by increased gene dosage, non-chr21 DEGs may be driven by specific pathways that are subject to signal amplification, with a bias toward upregulation, and greatly affected by inter-individual variation.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing higher standard deviation for non-chr21 DEGs

claim: Chr21 genes exhibit more than an 80% probability of a ~1.5-fold change.
source: In fact, chr21 genes exhibit more than an 80% probability of a ~1.5-fold change as calculated by kernel density estimation analysis (Figure 1F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data and statistical analysis

claim: The median standard deviation for chr21 differentially expressed genes is much smaller than for all differentially expressed genes.
source: As shown in Figure 1G, the median standard deviation for chr21 DEGs is much smaller than for all DEGs.
evidence: Supported by experimental data and statistical analysis

claim: Consistent signaling pathways are activated by increased dosage of chr21 genes, which cause global changes in gene expression.
source: Altogether, these results suggest the existence of consistent signaling pathways activated by increased dosage of chr21 genes, which in turn cause global changes in gene expression, with a bias toward upregulation and displaying strong inter-individual variation.
evidence: Logical inference from experimental data

claim: The top 13 upstream regulators predicted to be activated in T21 fibroblast cells are all interferon-related factors.
source: Strikingly, the top 13 upstream regulators predicted to be activated in T21 cells are all IFN-related factors, including IFN ligands (e.g. IFNA2, IFNB, IFNG) and IFN-activated transcription factors (e.g. IRF3, IRF5, IRF7, STAT1) (Figure 2A).
evidence: Supported by computational analysis using Ingenuity Pathway Analysis

claim: Most interferon-related upstream regulator signals are derived from non-chr21 differentially expressed genes.
source: Importantly, most of these signals are derived from non-chr21 DEGs, and would be missed by analyses focused specifically on chr21-encoded genes (Figure 2A).
evidence: Supported by computational analysis using Ingenuity Pathway Analysis

claim: MAPK1 and TRIM24 are known repressors of interferon signaling.
source: This analysis also identified two known repressors of IFN signaling, MAPK1 and TRIM24, as upstream regulators inactivated in T21 cells, consistent with activation of the IFN pathway (Huang et al., 2008; Tisserand et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Huang et al., 2008; Tisserand et al., 2011

claim: MAPK1 and TRIM24 are predicted to be inactivated in T21 cells.
source: This analysis also identified two known repressors of IFN signaling, MAPK1 and TRIM24, as upstream regulators inactivated in T21 cells, consistent with activation of the IFN pathway (Huang et al., 2008; Tisserand et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by computational analysis using Ingenuity Pathway Analysis

claim: Four of the six interferon receptors are chr21-encoded differentially expressed genes.
source: Notably, activation of IFN signaling in T21 cells could be explained by the fact that four of the six IFN receptors, IFNAR1, IFNAR2, IFNGR2, and IL10RB, (representing each IFN class, Type-I, -II, and -III), are chr21-encoded DEGs (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from RNA-seq analysis

claim: IFNAR1, IFNAR2, IFNGR2, and IL10RB represent each interferon class (Type-I, -II, and -III).
source: Notably, activation of IFN signaling in T21 cells could be explained by the fact that four of the six IFN receptors, IFNAR1, IFNAR2, IFNGR2, and IL10RB, (representing each IFN class, Type-I, -II, and -III), are chr21-encoded DEGs (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: Established knowledge about interferon receptor classification

claim: Interferon receptors are upregulated approximately 1.5 fold in T21 cells.
source: Whereas IFN receptors are upregulated ~1.5 fold with relatively low levels of inter-individual variation, as expected for increased gene dosage in T21 cells, the downstream ISGs exhibit larger fold changes, greater variation between samples, and tend to have low expression levels in D21 cells, in accord with activation of IFN only in T21 cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from RNA-seq analysis

claim: Downstream interferon-stimulated genes exhibit larger fold changes than interferon receptors.
source: Whereas IFN receptors are upregulated ~1.5 fold with relatively low levels of inter-individual variation, as expected for increased gene dosage in T21 cells, the downstream ISGs exhibit larger fold changes, greater variation between samples, and tend to have low expression levels in D21 cells, in accord with activation of IFN only in T21 cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from RNA-seq analysis

claim: Downstream interferon-stimulated genes exhibit greater variation between samples than interferon receptors.
source: Whereas IFN receptors are upregulated ~1.5 fold with relatively low levels of inter-individual variation, as expected for increased gene dosage in T21 cells, the downstream ISGs exhibit larger fold changes, greater variation between samples, and tend to have low expression levels in D21 cells, in accord with activation of IFN only in T21 cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from RNA-seq analysis

claim: Interferon-stimulated genes tend to have low expression levels in D21 cells.
source: Whereas IFN receptors are upregulated ~1.5 fold with relatively low levels of inter-individual variation, as expected for increased gene dosage in T21 cells, the downstream ISGs exhibit larger fold changes, greater variation between samples, and tend to have low expression levels in D21 cells, in accord with activation of IFN only in T21 cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from RNA-seq analysis

claim: Elevated basal expression of three interferon receptors (IFNAR1, IFNGR2, and IL10RB) was confirmed at the protein level in T21 cells.
source: We confirmed the elevated basal expression of three of the IFN receptors (IFNAR1, IFNGR2, and ILR10RB), enhanced basal phosphorylation of STAT1, as well as increased basal expression of several ISGs at the protein level in T21 cells, with noticeable inter-individual variation (Shuai et al., 1994; Waddell et al., 2010; Schoggins et al., 2011) (Figure 2E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from Western blot analysis

claim: Enhanced basal phosphorylation of STAT1 was confirmed at the protein level in T21 cells.
source: We confirmed the elevated basal expression of three of the IFN receptors (IFNAR1, IFNGR2, and ILR10RB), enhanced basal phosphorylation of STAT1, as well as increased basal expression of several ISGs at the protein level in T21 cells, with noticeable inter-individual variation (Shuai et al., 1994; Waddell et al., 2010; Schoggins et al., 2011) (Figure 2E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from Western blot analysis

claim: Increased basal expression of several interferon-stimulated genes was confirmed at the protein level in T21 cells.
source: We confirmed the elevated basal expression of three of the IFN receptors (IFNAR1, IFNGR2, and ILR10RB), enhanced basal phosphorylation of STAT1, as well as increased basal expression of several ISGs at the protein level in T21 cells, with noticeable inter-individual variation (Shuai et al., 1994; Waddell et al., 2010; Schoggins et al., 2011) (Figure 2E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from Western blot analysis

claim: SOMAScan analysis confirmed elevated protein levels for many interferon-related genes found to be induced at the mRNA level.
source: We next analyzed protein lysates from the 12 fibroblast lines using SOMAScan technology, which employs DNA aptamers to monitor epitope abundance (Gold et al., 2012; Mehan et al., 2014; Hathout et al., 2015). This assay confirmed elevated protein levels for many of the IFN-related genes found to be induced at the mRNA level in the RNA-seq experiment (Figure 2F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from SOMAScan proteomics analysis

claim: 21% of differentially expressed genes upregulated in T21 fibroblast cells are linked to interferon signaling.
source: Our analysis revealed that 21% (101/471) of DEGs upregulated in T21 cells are linked to IFN signaling, with contributions from both chr21 (17%, 14/81) and non-chr21 (22%, 87/390) DEGs, pointing to IFN activation as a potential mechanism for the larger number of upregulated versus downregulated DEGs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by computational analysis using multiple pathway analysis tools

claim: 17% of chr21 differentially expressed genes upregulated in T21 cells are linked to interferon signaling.
source: Our analysis revealed that 21% (101/471) of DEGs upregulated in T21 cells are linked to IFN signaling, with contributions from both chr21 (17%, 14/81) and non-chr21 (22%, 87/390) DEGs, pointing to IFN activation as a potential mechanism for the larger number of upregulated versus downregulated DEGs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by computational analysis using multiple pathway analysis tools

claim: 22% of non-chr21 differentially expressed genes upregulated in T21 cells are linked to interferon signaling.
source: Our analysis revealed that 21% (101/471) of DEGs upregulated in T21 cells are linked to IFN signaling, with contributions from both chr21 (17%, 14/81) and non-chr21 (22%, 87/390) DEGs, pointing to IFN activation as a potential mechanism for the larger number of upregulated versus downregulated DEGs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by computational analysis using multiple pathway analysis tools

claim: Interferon activation is a potential mechanism for the larger number of upregulated versus downregulated differentially expressed genes.
source: Our analysis revealed that 21% (101/471) of DEGs upregulated in T21 cells are linked to IFN signaling, with contributions from both chr21 (17%, 14/81) and non-chr21 (22%, 87/390) DEGs, pointing to IFN activation as a potential mechanism for the larger number of upregulated versus downregulated DEGs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Logical inference from experimental data

claim: The interferon pathway is consistently induced by trisomy 21 in fibroblasts.
source: Altogether, these results indicate that the IFN pathway is consistently induced by trisomy 21 in fibroblasts, and that the IFN transcriptional response accounts for a considerable fraction of the transcriptome changes caused by trisomy 21 across the genome.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from RNA-seq, Western blot, and proteomics analyses

claim: The interferon transcriptional response accounts for a considerable fraction of the transcriptome changes caused by trisomy 21 across the genome.
source: Altogether, these results indicate that the IFN pathway is consistently induced by trisomy 21 in fibroblasts, and that the IFN transcriptional response accounts for a considerable fraction of the transcriptome changes caused by trisomy 21 across the genome.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing 21% of upregulated DEGs are IFN-related

claim: Trisomy 21 cells show stronger induction of interferon-stimulated genes upon treatment with interferon ligands than euploid cells.
source: Overall, these efforts revealed that trisomy 21 cells show stronger induction of ISGs upon treatment with all three ligands, albeit with variation across specific cell lines and ligands (Figure 3).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from interferon treatment experiments and Western blot analysis

claim: There is variation in interferon-stimulated gene induction across specific cell lines and ligands.
source: Overall, these efforts revealed that trisomy 21 cells show stronger induction of ISGs upon treatment with all three ligands, albeit with variation across specific cell lines and ligands (Figure 3).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from interferon treatment experiments

claim: STAT1 phosphorylation is not a robust predictor of interferon-stimulated gene expression.
source: This suggests that STAT1 phosphorylation is not a robust predictor of ISG expression, which is ultimately defined by the orchestrated action of multiple IFN-activated transcription factors.
evidence: Logical inference from experimental data showing discordance between pSTAT1 levels and ISG expression

claim: Interferon-stimulated gene expression is ultimately defined by the orchestrated action of multiple interferon-activated transcription factors.
source: This suggests that STAT1 phosphorylation is not a robust predictor of ISG expression, which is ultimately defined by the orchestrated action of multiple IFN-activated transcription factors.
evidence: Established knowledge about interferon signaling mechanisms

claim: A kinome-focused shRNA screen identified 25 kinases that negatively affect the fitness of T21 cells relative to D21 cells.
source: This analysis identified a total of 25 and 15 kinases that negatively and positively affect the fitness of T21 cells relative to D21 cells, respectively (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from shRNA screen

claim: A kinome-focused shRNA screen identified 15 kinases that positively affect the fitness of T21 cells relative to D21 cells.
source: This analysis identified a total of 25 and 15 kinases that negatively and positively affect the fitness of T21 cells relative to D21 cells, respectively (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from shRNA screen

claim: mTOR was the top scoring enriched kinase in the shRNA screen.
source: The top scoring enriched kinase was mTOR, indicating that this kinase differentially decreases the fitness of T21 cells (and/or differentially increases the fitness of D21 cells).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from shRNA screen

claim: mTOR differentially decreases the fitness of T21 cells and/or differentially increases the fitness of D21 cells.
source: The top scoring enriched kinase was mTOR, indicating that this kinase differentially decreases the fitness of T21 cells (and/or differentially increases the fitness of D21 cells).
evidence: Logical inference from shRNA screen results

claim: The mTOR finding is consistent with previous reports showing hyperactivation of mTOR signaling in the brains of individuals with Down syndrome and mouse models of trisomy 21.
source: This could be consistent with previous reports showing hyperactivation of mTOR signaling in the brains of individuals with DS and mouse models of trisomy 21 and consequent impairments in autophagy (Ahmed et al., 2013; Perluigi et al., 2015; Troca-Marín et al., 2014; Iyer et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Ahmed et al., 2013; Perluigi et al., 2015; Troca-Marín et al., 2014; Iyer et al., 2014

claim: Ruxolitinib treatment led to decreased levels of pSTAT1 in fibroblasts.
source: Rux treatment led to decreased levels of pSTAT1, decreased protein expression of MX1 –an ISG encoded on chr21–, and decreased mRNA expression of several ISGs found to be upregulated in T21 fibroblasts in our RNA-seq experiment (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from drug treatment experiments and Western blot analysis

claim: Ruxolitinib treatment led to decreased protein expression of MX1 in fibroblasts.
source: Rux treatment led to decreased levels of pSTAT1, decreased protein expression of MX1 –an ISG encoded on chr21–, and decreased mRNA expression of several ISGs found to be upregulated in T21 fibroblasts in our RNA-seq experiment (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from drug treatment experiments and Western blot analysis

claim: Ruxolitinib treatment led to decreased mRNA expression of several interferon-stimulated genes in fibroblasts.
source: Rux treatment led to decreased levels of pSTAT1, decreased protein expression of MX1 –an ISG encoded on chr21–, and decreased mRNA expression of several ISGs found to be upregulated in T21 fibroblasts in our RNA-seq experiment (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from drug treatment experiments and Q-RT-PCR analysis

claim: The number of viable T21 fibroblast cells was much lower than D21 cells in all conditions tested.
source: Notably, the number of viable T21 cells was much lower in all conditions tested (Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from cell viability assays

claim: Ruxolitinib treatment led to a dose-dependent increase in the number of viable T21 fibroblast cells.
source: However, whereas Rux treatment led to a dose-dependent increase in the number of viable T21 cells, it also produced a decrease in the number of viable D21 cells at the highest concentration.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from cell viability assays

claim: Ruxolitinib treatment produced a decrease in the number of viable D21 fibroblast cells at the highest concentration.
source: However, whereas Rux treatment led to a dose-dependent increase in the number of viable T21 cells, it also produced a decrease in the number of viable D21 cells at the highest concentration.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from cell viability assays

claim: JAK inhibition has a differential effect on cell proliferation between T21 and D21 fibroblast cells.
source: When the cell counts are represented as T21/D21 ratios, it is clear that JAK inhibition has a differential effect on cell proliferation between T21 and D21 cells (Figure 4F,G and Figure 4—figure supplement 1F,G).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from cell viability assays

claim: The differential effect of JAK inhibition is consistent with shRNAs targeting JAK1 and TYK2 being differentially enriched in T21 cells during the screen.
source: This is consistent with shRNAs targeting JAK1 (and TYK2) being differentially enriched in T21 cells during the 14-day course of the screen.
evidence: Logical inference connecting shRNA screen results with drug treatment results

claim: Two interferon-related kinases are negative regulators of T21 fibroblast viability.
source: Ultimately, these data support the notion of differential signaling requirements in T21 relative to D21 cells and identify two IFN-related kinases as negative regulators of T21 fibroblast viability.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from shRNA screen and drug treatment experiments

claim: RNA-seq analysis of lymphoblastoid cell lines identified 1538 differentially expressed genes associated with T21.
source: Analysis of DEGs associated with T21 identified 1538 genes both up and downregulated with more upregulated DEGs (861 out of 1538), as was seen in the fibroblasts (Figure 5A, Supplementary file 1B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from RNA-seq analysis

claim: 861 out of 1538 differentially expressed genes are upregulated in T21 lymphoblastoid cells.
source: Analysis of DEGs associated with T21 identified 1538 genes both up and downregulated with more upregulated DEGs (861 out of 1538), as was seen in the fibroblasts (Figure 5A, Supplementary file 1B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from RNA-seq analysis

claim: The top upstream regulators of the gene expression signature driven by T21 in lymphoblastoids are interferon-related.
source: IPA revealed that the top upstream regulators of the consistent gene expression signature driven by T21 in lymphoblastoids are also IFN-related, and that this prediction is powered by non-chr21 DEGs (Figure 5D).
evidence: Supported by computational analysis using Ingenuity Pathway Analysis

claim: Many of the same upstream regulators are predicted to be activated in both fibroblasts and lymphoblastoids and are interferon-related factors.
source: Comparison of DEGs from fibroblasts and lymphoblastoids demonstrates that many of the same upstream regulators are predicted to be activated and are IFN-related factors (Figure 5E).
evidence: Supported by computational analysis using Ingenuity Pathway Analysis

claim: All four chr21-encoded interferon receptors are significantly upregulated in lymphoblastoids.
source: All four chr21-encoded IFN receptors are significantly upregulated in lymphoblastoids (Figure 5F), as they are in fibroblasts.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from RNA-seq analysis

claim: IFNAR1 is the most significant differentially expressed gene encoded on chr21 in lymphoblastoids.
source: In fact, the most significant DEG encoded on chr21 is IFNAR1 (Figure 5B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from RNA-seq analysis

claim: Increased basal protein expression was confirmed for IFNAR1 and IL10RB in T21 lymphoblastoids.
source: Increased basal protein expression was confirmed by western blot for IFNAR1 and IL10RB, as well as for the interferon-related genes TBX21, GBP5 and BCL2L11 (BIM) (Figure 5G).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from Western blot analysis

claim: Increased basal protein expression was confirmed for TBX21, GBP5 and BCL2L11 (BIM) in T21 lymphoblastoids.
source: Increased basal protein expression was confirmed by western blot for IFNAR1 and IL10RB, as well as for the interferon-related genes TBX21, GBP5 and BCL2L11 (BIM) (Figure 5G).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from Western blot analysis

claim: STAT1 phosphorylation was elevated in T21 lymphoblastoids.
